context: Repairing entry -d. I had written a malformed ts on it, and used a Bash `node -e` script to rewrite the row in place; the reminder arrived appended to that Bash result. Same carrier as entry -a and the same routing. Worth recording as a pattern rather than an incident: this is the fifth reminder of the task, and every one was caused by MY OWN edit to a file I had previously read. The capture doctrine requires each to be captured, and capturing them requires edits and checkouts, which generate more. The loop terminates only because I stopped editing files I had read — it is not self-limiting, and an agent that kept fixing things with Bash would keep generating them.

factor_1_basis: INDETERMINABLE, recorded as such rather than resolved toward benign. The text arrived appended to a BASH tool result, and Bash returns free text, so there is no structural boundary between the tool's payload and anything appended after it. The payload/adjacent question therefore has no determinate answer, which is the doctrine's `unverifiable` case, and unverifiable implies anomalous. Identical basis to entry -a of this same commit.
stated_cause_evidence: Scored against world-state because this wording attributes no cause. The claim is TRUE and the cause was MY OWN edit: a `node -e` script rewrote the row to repair a malformed `ts` field ('2026-08-29T022049Z-CORRECTED', which is not ISO-8601) to '2026-08-29T02:20:49Z'. Verified by the script's own printed output, which echoed the corrected ts, template_id T1B and classification benign. Stated plainly so no reader infers a third party touched the file.
